environment.description: Same application deployed on AKS cluster v1.28 with Pod Security Standards enforced at namespace level via label 'pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted'. The restricted profile mandates: runAsNonRoot=true, allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, drops ALL capabilities, seccompProfile type RuntimeDefault. Additionally, the namespace has a LimitRange object setting default container CPU limit to 200m and memory to 256Mi, with a ResourceQuota capping total namespace CPU to 1 core. The pod's seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault) restricts syscalls available to the .NET runtime, and the 200m CPU ceiling combined with Kubernetes CPU throttling via CFS bandwidth control ensures that any regex backtracking operation exceeding ~150ms of wall-clock compute per request cycle gets throttled to the point where the 30-second Regex timeout fires a RegexMatchTimeoutException before meaningful DoS amplification occurs, as the container cannot burst beyond its 200m CPU share. The CFS period is 100ms with quota of 20ms, meaning exponential backtracking that would normally consume 30 seconds of CPU in exploitable_env only gets 20ms of real compute per 100ms period, reducing effective throughput by 80% and causing the .NET regex engine's internal tick counter to still advance at wall-clock rate, triggering the timeout far before resource exhaustion of the node.
